subject: ventures/wordpress-plugin-review-check
auditor: agent session (Claude), quality round 113, see run record
professional: a senior WordPress.org Plugin Review Team member / experienced plugin developer who ships to the directory; they check first that the Stable tag rule matches what Plugin Check (PCP) and the readme docs say (including Stable tag: trunk), that 'escaped' means what WPCS EscapeOutput accepts, that the plugin header is parsed the way core's get_file_data() parses it, and that a GPL-compatible licence is actually validated rather than merely present

evidence.correctness: Sources the author did not write, fetched this session: WordPress/plugin-check trunk includes/Checker/Checks/Plugin_Repo/Plugin_Readme_Check.php (check_stable_tag, check_license), WordPress-Coding-Standards develop WordPress/Helpers/EscapingFunctionsTrait.php and Sniffs/Security/NonceVerificationSniff.php, wordpress-develop trunk src/wp-includes/functions.php get_file_data() (raw.githubusercontent.com, HTTP 200), plus developer.wordpress.org 'How your readme.txt works', 'Header requirements' and 'Detailed Plugin Guidelines' (WebFetch). Probe: node /tmp/claude-0/wp-audit/probe.mjs builds 19 fixture plugins under /tmp/claude-0/wp-audit/cases and runs the shipped runCheck(). Pass: Stable tag 1.0.0 vs Version 1.0.1 -> mismatch, ok false (PCP stable_tag_mismatch); matching 1.0.0/1.0.0 -> match, ok true; 'Stable Tag' capitalised read correctly; 'v1.0.0' vs '1.0.0' -> mismatch (PCP compares with !==, same). Fail: (1) 'Stable tag: trunk' -> ok true, status 'trunk' (PCP raises error trunk_stable_tag; readme docs: trunk 'neither supported nor recommended', 'prohibiting its use for new plugins'); (2) 'License: Proprietary' -> ok true (PCP invalid_license / license_mismatch; Guideline 1 requires GPL-compatible); (3) echo sanitize_text_field( $_GET['q'] ) -> clean, though sanitize_text_field, sanitize_email, sanitize_file_name and boolval are not in WPCS's escapingFunctions list; (4) '<?php' + '# Plugin Name: My Plugin' / '# Version: 1.0.0', and '<?php /* Plugin Name: My Plugin */' -> 'Plugin header: none found', ok false, though core's get_file_data regex '^(?:[ \t]*<\?(?:php)?)?[ \t\/*#@]*Name:' accepts both; (5) a plugin with admin/legacy.php carrying a stray 'Plugin Name:' comment -> header taken from admin/legacy.php and a false mismatch against Version '0.1 */' (core reads the main file from the plugin's top level and strips '*/' with _cleanup_header_comment); (6) a header that starts after 9,000 bytes is found, though get_file_data reads only the first 8 KB; (7) <?= $_GET['q'] ?> and echo esc_html( $title ) . $_GET['q'] -> clean (WPCS targets T_OPEN_TAG_WITH_ECHO and per-argument escaping). The core version compare is right; the surrounding rules diverge from the official tooling in both directions, so 2.
evidence.completeness: Each feature README.md, VENTURE.yaml, llms.txt and index.html name was run: Stable tag vs Version cross-check (match, mismatch, trunk), required readme fields (Stable tag, License, License URI) and header fields (Plugin Name, Version), recommended fields reported but not failing, line-level unescaped-superglobal check, file-level missing-nonce check, CLI with --readme, --plugin-file, --json and exit codes 0/1/2, browser page with the worked example, local usage counter with opt-out, three SEO pages. All work end to end as described (probe and the 72 tests); no stubs, TODOs or dead links found. served-copy: 'no placeholder or retired origin left'. It does what it says; what it says is narrow and partly wrong, scored under correctness, claims and domain.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/wordpress-plugin-review-check && node --test '*.test.mjs': tests 72, pass 72, fail 0 (also 'node --test' as the README says: 72 pass). Seven mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py on scan.mjs: dropping the mismatch gate from ok (scan.mjs:247) caught; dropping the missing-required-header gate (scan.mjs:249) SURVIVED; deleting the nonce-function skip (scan.mjs:183) caught; nonce finding line off by one (scan.mjs:188) SURVIVED; removing sanitize_text_field from the escaping list (scan.mjs:138) caught, because scan.test.mjs:126 pins sanitize_text_field as an escaping function, i.e. the suite locks in the WPCS departure; disabling the trunk branch (scan.mjs:218) caught, likewise pinning the trunk-is-fine rule PCP rejects; dropping 'print' from OUTPUT_STATEMENT (scan.mjs:139) SURVIVED. 3 of 7 survive; no fixture uses a '#'-style or one-line header or a nested file with 'Plugin Name:'.
evidence.craft: Read scan.mjs (267 lines), check.mjs (232), index.html script, scan.test.mjs, check.test.mjs, page.test.mjs. One pure, dependency-free module shared by CLI and browser, clear doc comments stating the heuristic limits, sensible CLI exit codes. Defects: the header parser re-implements get_file_data with a narrower prefix class ([*/] instead of core's <?php + [ \t/*#@]), no '*/' cleanup and no 8 KB window (scan.mjs:77-88); header search walks every subdirectory and takes the first readdir hit (scan.mjs:98, check.mjs:39-66), where core reads top-level files only; readme field regexes match anywhere in the file, not only the header block before the first '==' section; nonce detection matches function names inside comments ('// TODO wp_verify_nonce( ) later' clears a file). A senior JS reviewer would accept the style; the parsing fidelity gaps are logged as defects.
evidence.claims: Backed: no-upload (page.test.mjs checks no network call; index.html reads files with File API), CLI makes no network call (check.mjs imports only node:fs/node:path/node:url), not-affiliated and trademark notice and no-warranty text on all four pages (index.html:345, :356; vs-plugin-check.html footer; stable-tag-mismatch.html footer), 'evidence, not a determination' and line/file-level heuristic limits stated in README and pages, vs-plugin-check.html's description of Plugin Check (needs a WordPress install, runs from Tools or 'wp plugin check') matches its wordpress.org listing. Unbacked or contradicted: README.md:19 and check.mjs:159 call License URI a 'hard requirement', but the readme docs mark License URI '(OPTIONAL)' and PCP does not check it; stable-tag-mismatch.html:60-61 says Stable tag: trunk is 'a valid, if less common, choice' while the docs say it is discouraged and prohibited for new plugins and PCP errors on it; index.html:50/:323 and README.md:30 say plugin review 'looks for a nonce check anywhere in a file', but WPCS NonceVerification checks the enclosing function scope; README.md:19 says a GPL-compatible licence 'must be declared' but the tool accepts any value; llms.txt:5 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in' is calculator boilerplate on a file checker. 2.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job as a developer preparing a first submission: on a conventional /** */ header the tool gives a fast, correct Stable tag/Version answer with no WordPress install, and works as a CI gate (exit 1 on mismatch). But the official Plugin Check is free, is what the review team runs, and covers these checks with closer rules, and this tool would pass a submission PCP rejects (trunk stable tag, non-GPL licence, sanitize_text_field used as output escaping), while missing PCP readme errors a reviewer hits in the first hour: more than 5 tags (too_many_tags), short description over 150 characters (trimmed_short_description), outdated Tested up to, readme/header plugin-name mismatch, readme vs header licence mismatch, Requires at least/Requires PHP read from the header. VENTURE.yaml stage prototype, mrr null; it links to no paid product, so under the 2026-11-24 direction it is a demoted free tool with no front door role.
evidence.domain: Compared against PCP's Plugin_Readme_Check (trunk), WPCS 3.x EscapeOutput/NonceVerification, core get_file_data(), and developer.wordpress.org readme and header docs. Matches: Stable tag must equal Version exactly (PCP stable_tag_mismatch, !==); Plugin Name is the only required header (Header requirements page); escaping list mostly mirrors WPCS (esc_*, wp_kses*, absint, intval, floatval, rawurlencode, wp_json_encode, number_format). Departs: trunk Stable tag treated as fine (PCP error); License presence, not validity, checked (PCP SPDX/GPL validation); License URI made required (docs: optional); Version made required (not required by the Header requirements page, though needed for the cross-check); readme 'Requires at least' reported as recommended though since WP 5.8 the directory reads it from the plugin header; sanitize_* accepted as escaping (not in WPCS list); $_GET/$_REQUEST/$_FILES not considered for nonce (WPCS warns on $_GET/$_REQUEST and errors on $_FILES); file-level instead of scope-level nonce check; core header syntax ('#', '<?php /* ... */', 8 KB window, top-level main file) not followed. A senior reviewer would sign off on the Stable tag compare only.

defects.what: 'Stable tag: trunk' passes (ok true, '[i]' note) and the page calls it 'a valid, if less common, choice'. Plugin Check raises error trunk_stable_tag and the readme docs say trunk is neither supported nor recommended and prohibited for new plugins, so a developer gated on this tool submits a readme PCP rejects.

Any License value passes (License: Proprietary -> ok true), though README.md:19 says a GPL-compatible licence must be declared and PCP raises invalid_license / license_mismatch; Guideline 1 is the directory's first hard rule.

sanitize_text_field, sanitize_email, sanitize_file_name and boolval count as output escaping; WPCS EscapeOutput (what PCP runs) does not accept them, so 'echo sanitize_text_field( $_GET[...] )' reports clean. scan.test.mjs:126 pins the departure.

Plugin header parsing departs from core get_file_data(): '#'-prefixed and '<?php /* Plugin Name: ... */' headers are not found (false 'none found', exit 1); '*/' is not stripped (Version '0.1 */'); no 8 KB window; the header file is the first readdir hit in any subdirectory, so a nested file with 'Plugin Name:' wins and yields a false mismatch.
License URI is treated as a required readme field and missing it fails the check with 'hard requirement' text, but the readme docs mark License URI optional and PCP does not check it.

Nonce check is file-level and textual: a nonce call in another function, or only in a comment, clears a $_POST read; $_GET/$_REQUEST/$_FILES are not considered. WPCS NonceVerification is scope-based and covers those superglobals. Disclosed as a heuristic, but index.html:323 and README.md:30 say this is how plugin review itself checks.

Readme rules PCP errors or warns on in the first hour are not checked: more than 5 tags, short description over 150 characters, outdated Tested up to, readme/header plugin-name mismatch, readme/header licence mismatch; readme 'Requires at least' is suggested though the directory reads it from the header since WP 5.8.

3 of 7 seeded mutants survive (dropping the missing-required-header gate from ok, nonce line off by one, dropping 'print' from output statements); no fixture covers '#'/one-line headers, nested header files, trunk-as-error or licence validity, and two tests pin rules that depart from PCP/WPCS.
Claims: 'Plugin review looks for a nonce check anywhere in a file' (WPCS checks function scope) and 'License URI ... hard requirement' are not backed by WordPress.org sources.
llms.txt says 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in', calculator boilerplate that does not describe a file checker.

verdict: Does not meet the bar (correctness 2, claims 2, verification 2, median 2); finished (completeness 3). Every feature it lists runs end to end, the 72 tests pass, and the core Stable tag vs Version compare agrees with Plugin Check's stable_tag_mismatch rule. Against Plugin Check's own source, WPCS and core get_file_data(), all fetched this session, the surrounding rules go wrong both ways. It passes plugins Plugin Check rejects: Stable tag trunk, a proprietary licence, echo sanitize_text_field($_GET[...]), a nonce call only in a comment. It fails plugins WordPress accepts: '#' or one-line headers, a missing License URI (optional per the readme docs), a stray header in a subdirectory. It also skips readme checks a reviewer hits early (5-tag limit, 150-character short description). 3 of 7 seeded mutants survive, and two tests lock in the departures. Disclaimers, the no-upload claim and the Plugin Check comparison are honest. Two page claims (trunk is valid, file-level nonce is how review checks) contradict the sources. It is a demoted free tool that does not lead to any paid product.
